components.name: Button
components.summary: A native action button with explicit variants and safe pending behavior.
components.usage: Use for actions. Use a link for navigation. Keep a visible accessible name; choose type=submit explicitly inside forms. Native button props and refs are forwarded.
components.accessibility: Uses a native button and visible focus. Pending disables activation and sets aria-busy; preserve meaningful button text while work is pending.

props.name: children
props.meaning: Visible action name or content with an equivalent accessible name.

props.name: type
props.meaning: Native form behavior; the safe default does not submit a form.

props.name: variant
props.meaning: Semantic action emphasis, styled through product-owned tokens.

props.name: pending
props.meaning: Disables activation and exposes aria-busy while the caller owns pending work.

props.name: …buttonProps
props.meaning: Native props such as disabled, onClick, className, ref and ARIA attributes are forwarded.

examples.label: Action states and product styling
examples.description: Local actions, disabled and pending states, and a scoped token override.

components.name: TextField
components.summary: A labeled native input with linked hints and validation messages.
components.usage: Use for a single native input with a persistent label. The caller owns value, validation and submission. Keep domain-specific validation and credentials in the feature; use other native controls for multiline text or selection.
components.accessibility: Associates label and input through a stable id; links hint and error descriptions and sets aria-invalid for errors. Native required, disabled, ref and keyboard behavior are preserved. The feature owns dynamic error summaries or announcements.

props.name: type
props.meaning: Supports text, email, password, search, tel, url, number and native date/time inputs. Use separate native controls for checkbox, radio, file, range or other selection behavior.

props.name: label
props.meaning: Persistent accessible label; a placeholder cannot replace it.

props.name: id
props.meaning: Optional DOM id; a stable useId value is generated when absent.

props.name: hint
props.meaning: Optional help linked to the input through aria-describedby.

props.name: error
props.meaning: Caller-owned validation message linked to the input; also marks it invalid.

props.name: …inputProps
props.meaning: Native value/defaultValue, onChange, type, required, disabled, className, ref and ARIA props are forwarded. Existing aria-describedby references are retained.

examples.label: Labeled input and validation
examples.description: Synthetic form input with a hint, validation message and disabled state.
examples.code:
<TextField label="Name" hint="Shown to your colleagues." required />
<TextField label="Email" type="email" error="Enter an email address." />

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A native checkbox with a persistent label and an optional mixed state.
components.usage: Use for independent on/off choices and for select-all controls whose options are partly chosen. The checked value stays caller-owned. Native input props and refs are forwarded.
components.accessibility: The native input stays focusable and announced while a drawn box shows checked, mixed, focus and disabled states; the whole label toggles it. indeterminate sets the native mixed state that assistive technology reports.

props.name: label
props.meaning: Visible label that names the checkbox.

props.name: indeterminate
props.meaning: Shows the mixed state, for example when only some options are chosen.

props.name: …inputProps
props.meaning: Native props such as checked, onChange, disabled, name and ref are forwarded.

examples.label: Checkbox states
examples.description: Checked, mixed and disabled examples held locally.

components.name: ErrorNotice
components.summary: Displays a public API failure message and an optional reload action.

props.name: error
props.meaning: Mapped through the shared public failure-message boundary.

props.name: operation
props.meaning: Selects the failure wording; failed or lost writes are reported as unknown outcomes. Defaults to read.

props.name: messages
props.meaning: Module-specific wording for its own stable error codes.

props.name: onReload
props.meaning: Optional recovery action when current data can be refreshed.

props.name: reloadLabel
props.meaning: Accessible name of the reload action; defaults to Reload.

components.accessibility: Uses role=alert so the failure is announced; the optional reload control is a native button.
components.usage: Pass the original error to preserve stable-code mapping. Offer reload only when the current data can be refreshed, and never imply that an unknown write outcome failed.

examples.label: Unavailable service with reload
examples.description: A synthetic SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE response; no live request is involved.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: A non-modal surface in the browser's top layer, placed next to an anchor element.
components.usage: Use for small panels tied to a control, such as filters or details, that should not be clipped by scrolling containers. The caller owns open and closes it from onClose. Content renders only while open, so its local state starts fresh each time. Use a page or form for long workflows.
components.accessibility: Uses the native popover attribute with role=dialog (or menu) and an aria-label. Opening focuses the element marked data-autofocus, or the popover itself. Escape, an outside click or another popover closes it; focus that would otherwise be lost returns to returnFocus or the anchor.

props.name: anchor
props.meaning: Element the popover is placed below, or above when only that fits.

props.name: open / onClose
props.meaning: Caller-owned visibility; onClose reports Escape, outside clicks and other popovers.

props.name: label
props.meaning: Accessible name of the popover.

props.name: returnFocus
props.meaning: Receives focus when the popover closes with focus inside it.

props.name: role
props.meaning: Semantic role of the surface.

props.name: align
props.meaning: Aligns the popover with the anchor's start or end edge.

props.name: children
props.meaning: Content rendered while open.

states: Open above when only that fits
Dismissed by Escape or an outside click

examples.label: Anchored details
examples.description: A button toggles synthetic details; no request is made.
examples.code:
<Button ref={setAnchor} onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>Details</Button>
<Popover anchor={anchor} open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} label="Details">…</Popover>

components.name: Menu
components.summary: A button that opens a list of actions in a Popover.
components.usage: Use for a few secondary actions attached to a control, such as column options. Each item's onSelect runs as the menu closes; pass checked for items with an on/off state and disabled for unavailable ones. Trigger props such as className, ref and data attributes are forwarded.
components.accessibility: The trigger is a labeled button with aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded. Items use menuitem or menuitemcheckbox roles. Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens on the first item and ArrowUp on the last; arrow keys, Home and End move between enabled items; Escape returns focus to the trigger and Tab closes the menu.

props.name: label
props.meaning: Names the trigger and the menu; also the trigger's tooltip.

props.name: items
props.meaning: Items with a stable key, label and onSelect, plus optional icon, checked and disabled.

props.name: children
props.meaning: Trigger content, usually an icon.

props.name: align
props.meaning: Aligns the menu with the trigger's start or end edge.

props.name: …buttonProps
props.meaning: Native trigger props such as className, ref and data attributes are forwarded.

examples.label: Secondary actions
examples.description: One available and one disabled synthetic action; no request is made.
examples.code:
<Menu label="Store actions" items={[{ key: "rename", label: "Rename", onSelect: rename }]}>
  <MoreIcon />
</Menu>

components.name: MultiSelectList
components.summary: A searchable list for choosing several options, with select-all, that renders only the options in view.
components.usage: Use when people choose several values from a long list, such as a column filter. Options keep their display order and a stable value; the selection set stays caller-owned. Search ignores case and accents; pass query and onQueryChange when the caller needs the search, and use searchOptions to find the same matches. Select all applies to the options the search found.
components.accessibility: Composes TextField for the search and Checkbox for select-all, which shows a mixed state when only some options are chosen. The options form a listbox with aria-multiselectable, aria-activedescendant and aria-setsize/aria-posinset, so arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End reach every option while only those in view are rendered; Space toggles the active option, and ArrowDown moves from the search into the list.

props.name: label
props.meaning: Accessible name of the option list.

props.name: locale
props.meaning: Language of the search and select-all labels, and of search matching.

props.name: options
props.meaning: Options with a stable value and a label, in display order. Keep the array stable between renders.

props.name: selected / onChange
props.meaning: Caller-owned chosen values.

props.name: query / onQueryChange
props.meaning: Optional controlled search text.

props.name: height
props.meaning: Maximum height of the scrolling list in pixels.

states: Keyboard focus on the active option

examples.label: Searchable choices
examples.description: Synthetic cities chosen locally; no request is made.

components.name: DataGrid
components.summary: A virtualized grid that sorts, filters and resizes columns over the rows it receives, with single or multiple selection.
components.usage: Use for lists of records that people scan, sort and filter in the browser; DataSet adds the CRUD toolbar and form. Give each column a value to sort and filter by. Sorting and filtering apply to the rows passed in, so a paginated caller sorts and filters only the loaded page; server-side sorting and filtering are not provided. Keep rows and columns stable between renders. Selection stays caller-owned. Pass exportName to offer Excel, CSV and PDF exports of the rows shown.
components.accessibility: Uses role=grid with aria-rowcount and aria-rowindex, so assistive technology knows the full size while only the rows in view are rendered. Rows expose aria-selected (aria-multiselectable with multiple) and form one tab stop: arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End move between rows, Enter activates and Space selects. Column headers expose aria-sort; their sort button, options Menu and a separator that Left/Right arrows resize are keyboard reachable, and the options appear on hover or focus. A live status reports the shown, total and selected counts. The Export menu is a labeled Menu; it is busy while a file is prepared, and a failure is announced as an alert.

props.name: label
props.meaning: Accessible name of the grid.

props.name: locale
props.meaning: Language of the grid labels, sorting and number formatting.

props.name: rows
props.meaning: All rows to show. Keep the array stable between renders.

props.name: columns
props.meaning: Stable key and header; value enables sorting and filtering, render overrides the formatted value, format names values, and width, minWidth, align, sortable, filterable and resizable tune the column. Keep the array stable between renders.

props.name: rowId
props.meaning: Stable row identity.

props.name: selectedId / onSelect
props.meaning: The current row. With single selection it is the highlighted row; clicking a row or moving with the arrow keys calls onSelect.

props.name: multiple
props.meaning: Allows choosing several rows: Ctrl/⌘ toggles a row, Shift selects a range, Space toggles the focused row and Ctrl/⌘+A selects every shown row.

props.name: selectedIds / onSelectedIdsChange
props.meaning: Caller-owned multiple selection; used only with multiple.

props.name: onRowActivate
props.meaning: Double-click or Enter on a row.

props.name: exportName
props.meaning: Offers an Export menu in the footer with Excel (.xlsx), CSV and PDF files of the rows the grid shows, in their order and with its filters; the name titles the files. Omit it where records must not leave the screen.

props.name: empty
props.meaning: Shown instead of the grid when there are no rows.

states: Filtered, with the filter shown on the header
Many rows (only those in view rendered)

examples.label: Ten thousand rows
examples.description: Synthetic screens generated locally; the example passes multiple, so Ctrl/⌘ and Shift choose several rows, and exportName, so the footer exports them. Sorting, filtering, resizing and exports make no request.
examples.code:
<DataGrid label="Screens" locale="en-US" rows={screens} columns={columns} rowId={(row) => row.id}
  multiple selectedIds={selected} onSelectedIdsChange={setSelected} exportName="Screens" />

components.name: DataSet
components.summary: Record-oriented CRUD presentation: a toolbar, a DataGrid and a caller-rendered form.

props.name: label
props.meaning: Accessible name of the dataset region and its grid.

props.name: locale
props.meaning: Language of the toolbar and grid labels.

props.name: mode
props.meaning: Caller-owned view; keep it in the URL when it identifies the page state.

props.name: rows
props.meaning: Records of the current page, already authorized by the API. Keep the array stable between renders.

props.name: columns
props.meaning: Stable key and header; value enables sorting and filtering, render overrides the formatted value, format names values, and width, minWidth, align, sortable, filterable and resizable tune the column. Keep the array stable between renders.

props.name: rowId
props.meaning: Stable record identity.

props.name: selectedId / onSelect
props.meaning: The current row. With single selection it is the highlighted row; clicking a row or moving with the arrow keys calls onSelect.

props.name: multiple
props.meaning: Allows choosing several rows: Ctrl/⌘ toggles a row, Shift selects a range, Space toggles the focused row and Ctrl/⌘+A selects every shown row.

props.name: selectedIds / onSelectedIdsChange
props.meaning: Caller-owned multiple selection; used only with multiple.

props.name: onModeChange, onAdd, onDuplicate, onRefresh
props.meaning: Toolbar actions; an omitted handler disables its button, for example while a draft is unsaved. Double-click or Enter on a row selects it and requests form mode.

props.name: onDelete
props.meaning: Omit when the records cannot be deleted; null shows the action disabled.

props.name: refreshing
props.meaning: Marks the refresh action busy while the caller reloads data.

props.name: exportName
props.meaning: Offers an Export menu in the toolbar with Excel (.xlsx), CSV and PDF files of the rows the grid shows, in their order and with its filters; the name titles the files. Omit it where records must not leave the screen.

props.name: empty
props.meaning: Grid content when there are no rows.

props.name: children
props.meaning: The current record's form, rendered only in form mode.

components.accessibility: The toolbar uses role=toolbar with labeled icon buttons and tooltips. The grid follows DataGrid: rows show selection only through color and aria-selected, are reached with the arrow keys, and Enter opens the form like a double-click. Links and buttons inside cells keep their own behavior. The Export menu is a labeled Menu; it is busy while a file is prepared, and a failure is announced as an alert.
components.usage: Keep records, selection, mode, API calls, permissions and draft handling in the feature. Pass handlers only for actions the API supports and the person may perform, and withhold onSelect and navigation while a form has unsaved changes. Sorting, filters and column widths persist while the dataset switches modes; previous and next follow the order the grid shows. Enable multiple only where several records can be acted on together. Pass exportName to offer exports; columns without a value are left out, numbers stay numeric in Excel, and CSV uses the locale's separator and decimal mark.

examples.label: Grid and form modes
examples.description: Synthetic local records with single selection, as on the companies page; selection and mode are held by the example and no request is made. A screen that acts on several records at once passes multiple; DataGrid's example shows it.
examples.code:
<DataSet label="Stores" locale="en-US" mode={mode} rows={stores} columns={columns}
  rowId={(row) => row.id} selectedId={selected} onSelect={setSelected} onModeChange={setMode}
  exportName="Stores">
  <StoreForm id={selected} />
</DataSet>

// Only where a screen acts on several records at once:
<DataSet multiple selectedIds={chosen} onSelectedIdsChange={setChosen} {...props} />
